statement: A readable medieval cosmography fixes Fire=hot/dry, Air=hot/moist, Water=moist/cold and Earth=cold/dry.
Medieval alchemical manuscripts link written instructions to drawings of vessels and furnaces.
Fourteenth-century alchemical visualization includes diverse processes and stages of transformation in vessels.
MS.140 is an early-fifteenth-century Italian Latin/Italian alchemical compilation with medical and alchemical waters, recipes, distillation and sublimation.
MS.140 contains small pen drawings of distilling apparatus within text and in a margin.
A fourteenth-century alchemical apparatus image carries the readable scroll label Distilatio Aceti.
The Arnald diagram orders Water, Air, Fire and Earth and gives directions for separating the stone in four stages.
A five-circle volvelle is inscribed with compound quality states and repeats calidum et humidum.
